author: Latin Business Daily
title: Inapi extends deadlines for industrial property procedures in areas affected by storms
text:
Inapi extends deadlines for industrial property procedures in areas affected by storms
The National Institute of Industrial Property (Inapi) announced on July 22 an extraordinary extension of statutory deadlines for administrative procedures managed by the institution. The measure benefits users residing in the Province of Huasco and throughout the Region of Coquimbo whose deadlines fall between July 20 and August 20, 2026.
According to Exempt Resolution No. 287 dated July 21, 2026, Inapi adopted this determination following the declaration of a State of Constitutional Catastrophe Exception in Huasco Province (Atacama Region) and all of Coquimbo Region. The state was decreed by the Ministry of Interior due to a severe weather front that caused flooding, isolation, and significant interruptions to basic services.
The extension applies automatically to all applicants, interested parties, and representatives with registered addresses within the zones under catastrophe status. Specifically, it covers statutory deadlines expiring within thirty days from publication of Supreme Decree No. 112 in the Official Gazette—between July 20 and August 20, 2026.
The granted extension is equal to half the time originally set for each procedure. This provides users with the maximum additional period authorized by Article 26 of Law No. 19.880 on Administrative Procedures Bases. The aim is to ensure legal certainty for users who are unable to access Inapi’s electronic processing system due to climate emergencies or connectivity failures.
For contentious cases handled before Inapi during this period, affected parties domiciled in these areas retain their legal right to claim procedural hindrance, according to general rules governing such judicial proceedings.
